title: ops corners weekly slate - Ravi journal
content:
Context: quick prep for the 11:00 weekly engineering sync (serving runtime + infra + console). Goal: reduce meeting time to 35m, surface only blockers and decisions, leave implementation nitpicks to async threads. This is a personal scratchpad to be handed off to Noah for agenda polish before standup.

Meeting date: 2026-03-10
Attendees to nudge: Noah (console), Hannah (infra), Marta (runtime), Samir (on-call/ops), Arjun (release eng - invite if rollout spikes)

High-level:
- One-line health: latency median + p95 trending; partial KV-cache hit improvement from last deploy; Console feature flag for rollout ready but UX issue remains.
- Biggest risk: canary rollback logic not respecting fallback route on region fail (seen twice in staging).

Proposed short agenda (35m):
1) Quick health snapshot (3m) — Hannah (infra): recent p50/p95 deltas, any emerging host OOMs
2) Canary / fallback decision (10m) — Marta + Samir: decide whether to gate next canary by region/tenant tier or pause rollout
3) Console follow-up (7m) — Noah: two UX bugs blocking sales demo; prioritize or ship workaround?
4) Capacity and burst policy reminder (5m) — Ravi: check Dedicated pool buffer for weekend traffic spike
5) Action items & owners (5m) — capture and confirm
6) Parking lot / async threads (remaining time)

Prep notes / quick data: (paste latest numbers during meeting)
- p50 today: 32ms (+4ms vs last week)
- p95 today: 215ms (+28ms) — spike appears correlated with long-tail KV cache misses on sequence lengths >1024
- Canary failures: 2 incidents in staging in past 48h; both due to fallback router misrouting to retired model alias (INF-4123)

Open questions to resolve in meeting:
- Do we prioritize a config-level fix (runtime) or a defensive router check (platform) for the fallback bug? Pros/cons noted below.
- Console UX: hold for polish or ship with tooltip workaround for demo? Quick wins: temporarily toggle feature flag + add banner.
- Is Dedicated pool buffer (burst) currently set to 20% or 30% for customer X? I think 20% but need confirmation from quota sheet.

Decision tradeoffs (short):
- Runtime config fix: more thorough, needs PR + rollout (2-3 days), fewer future surprises.
- Router defensive check: smaller change, hotfixable in ~4 hrs, but could be brittle across model alias changes.

Action items (compact lines for copy/paste into meeting notes):
- AI-001: Marta Li - Open PR for runtime fallback validation (start: 2026-03-10) - due 2026-03-15 - link to draft in linked_artifacts when available
- AI-002: Samir Kapoor - Create temporary router guard (hotfix) and deploy to staging for 4-day soak - due 2026-03-11
- AI-003: Noah Patel - Draft console workaround banner + feature flag toggle flow for sales demo; share copy with marketing - due 2026-03-12
- AI-004: Ravi Menon - Verify Dedicated pool burst percent for customer X; update capacity sheet and ping sales - due 2026-03-11 - sheet: https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/cc-capacity-2026
- AI-005: Hannah Chen - Share p95 breakdown by sequence length and host histograms pre-meeting - due 2026-03-10 (before 11:00)
- AI-006: Marta Li + Release Eng - Confirm canary gating policy adjustments and add rollout test for alias rotations - due 2026-03-17

Notes to self / rambling (keep):
- If we go with hotfix, ensure we tag the incident in SLO tracking so we can correlate any customer impact to deploys.
- Follow-up: add a short demo checklist for console-facing sales demos so we don't scramble on UX toggles. Keep it in Confluence page (linked_artifacts).
- Consider adding a lightweight canary simulation job to run alias-rotation scenarios nightly (low priority backlog item).

Parking lot (not for this meeting):
- UX: rework model selection flow in console (larger spike; schedule separate deep-dive).
- Optimize KV cache heuristics: experiment with sequence-length bucketing to reduce miss rate for long sequences.

Pre-meeting asks for attendees (copy these into calendar invite):
- Hannah: paste p50/p95 and host error rate 1h before standup
- Marta: link to PR draft or short note whether runtime or router fix is preferred
- Noah: bring two screenshots of console banner + link to demo customer flow
- Samir: confirm on-call availability for fast rollback if we choose to unpause canary

End-of-meeting quick template to paste in notes (to capture decisions):
- Decision: [runtime|router|pause]
- Owners: [comma-separated]
- Follow-up PRs: [links]
- Soak policy: [hours/days]
- Next check-in: [date/time]

Random/loose ideas to iterate later:
- Small CLI tool for quick canary pause+audit (single command) to reduce cognitive load during incidents.
- Add a console 'safe-mode' banner that flips a client-side flag to force fallback models for demos.

Ok — handoff to Noah for final agenda. Will watch action items after meeting and nudge owners as needed.

-- Ravi
